item.title: index
item.description: United Kingdom 1919–1945 The period from the close of the First World War to the end of the Second World War was one of profound transformation for the United Kingdom.

item.title: The Colonial Problem (RIIA, 1937)
item.description: Chatham House study-group report (Harold Nicolson chair; Margaret Bryant drafting) on the colonial question as international, administrative, and economic problem, written against the 1930s have/have-not controversy over transfer of colonies.

item.title: Survey of International Affairs, 1936
item.description: Arnold Toynbee's Royal Institute of International Affairs annual survey for 1936 — the Rhineland reoccupation, world rearmament, the end of the gold bloc, the Spanish Civil War, and the League's retreat from collective security.

item.title: Survey of International Affairs, 1925, Volume I — The Islamic World since the Peace Settlement
item.description: Arnold Toynbee's RIIA survey (issued 1927) of the Islamic world from the peace settlement through 1925–26: abolition of the Ottoman Caliphate, secularization, the Rif war, Egypt and the Sudan, Ibn Sa'ud and the Hijaz, the Syria–Palestine mandates, and the Mosul award.

item.title: Survey of International Affairs, 1926
item.description: Arnold Toynbee's RIIA survey (issued 1928) completing the post-Versailles record through 1926: Germany's admission to the League, inter-Allied debts, the international steel cartel, and the Chinese civil war down to the Shanghai Defence Force.

item.title: The World in March 1939 (Survey of International Affairs 1939–1946)
item.description: Opening volume of the RIIA wartime Survey (Toynbee and Ashton-Gwatkin, 1952): a political and economic snapshot of the world in March 1939 — world powers, Japan's and Germany's fields of aggression, comparative industrial strength, and Martin Wight on the balance of power — written after Nuremberg with the captured archives.

item.title: Survey of International Affairs, 1927
item.description: Arnold Toynbee's RIIA survey (issued 1929) for 1927: failure of the League Preparatory Commission and the Three-Power Geneva naval conference, German occupied territory and Thoiry, Fascist Italy's European policy, the Anglo-Soviet breach, the Kuomintang split, and U.S.–Mexico–Nicaragua.

item.title: Survey of International Affairs, 1931
item.description: Arnold Toynbee's RIIA survey (issued 1932) of the *annus terribilis*: world financial crisis from Credit-Anstalt through Britain's abandonment of gold, Hodson on the monetary outcome of the peace, the Austro-German customs-union project, and the Sino-Japanese conflict in Manchuria.

item.title: The Heartland
item.description: The Heartland The Heartland was the name given, at the close of the First World War, to the great interior of the Eurasian “World-Island”—the closed land mass of Europe, Asia, and Africa seen as one—whose command was held to decide world power in an age when the Columbian epoch of open oceanic expan...

item.title: Cabinet Dictatorship
item.description: Cabinet Dictatorship Cabinet dictatorship, in the interwar diagnosis of how Britain was actually governed, was the concentration of real power in a Cabinet sustained by rigid party organisation, so that the House of Commons became little more than a registering machine for decisions taken elsewhere.
